CTRL15-PRISON-ROOT-01 — scoped authored completion for Mental Prison only. On actual admission of one cast's prison to one recipient, after the initial save and entry-preventing defenses and before its entry damage, create one damage root owned by the original Mental Prison caster. Capture nullNonlethal from that dealer's actual unsuppressed Null Veil state at this creation event under the existing Null Veil contract. Record the cast, application, recipient, root and one unspent exit entitlement. No admitted prison means no entry damage root or deferred exit entitlement. The entry and eventual exit are two distinct damage events under this same root, not a combined hit and not two new casts. The exit inherits the stored nullNonlethal flag: later gaining, losing or suppressing the caster's Veil does not recapture it. Caster death or removal from the live initiative roster does not delete that root's original dealer identity or change the stored flag. Apply current recipient state and current applicable damage defenses separately at each actual packet; Wounds, concentration and life-state consequences remain event-local. This introduces no new class proc or resource permission and does not generalize Spectral Army's explicitly separate later-discharge roots.

Before any exit damage, atomically consume that application's exit entitlement and mark departure in progress. Duplicate cleanup, concurrent departure reasons and reentrant damage/death callbacks cannot emit another exit. A true entry-death or independently established target death/removal ends the application without an exit packet; zero HP without actual death is not itself this exception. Source-disabling suppression or an eligible source-disabling removal consumes the entitlement without creating an exit damage event or rolling exit dice. A suppressed prison that lawfully resumes uses the same original root and boundary; it restores neither entry damage nor the consumed exit. Complete an already admitted departure event without recursive cleanup; ordinary eligible packet prevention and the existing damage/life response sequence still apply.

Replacement follows the ordinary casting transaction before any source-specific replacement rule. If the NEW caster was maintaining the OLD prison, committing another concentration spell already ends that old concentration before the new spell's counter window, save or admission. Its legitimate unsuppressed old exit resolves as that independent ending; a later counter, successful new save or blocked new application never restores it. The statement that a saved-against attempt replaces nothing refers only to replacement-by-admission, not this earlier concentration displacement. If another caster's old prison still exists, a newly failed-save and otherwise admissible application first fully resolves the old departure and its ordinary responses; then rechecks the same recipient's continuing life/identity, the new cast's continuing concentration/source availability and its actual admission predicates. Do not reroll the new admission save, choose a replacement recipient, refund payment or create the new root/entry if those predicates now fail. Only a still-legal new admission creates its own distinct root using its own caster's state at that later admission. Thus old exit and new entry retain their separate event order and may have different root flags.

The exact True Seeing bridge already selected in Illusion/Perception14 Exact13 is a recognition/mental-departure interaction, not a dispel or source-disabling suppression. When that exact bridge actually applies to this still-admitted prison, use the same one live exit entitlement and stored root. A previously consumed entitlement produces no further damage. This adopts no other illusion bypass and supplies no missing Mental Prison or True Seeing acquisition. The full Control15 candidate remains pending its separate complete acceptance; this paragraph settles only the named causality/termination integration.

CTRL15-PUPPET-END-01 — scoped authored completion for Puppet Strings only. Record the two original future movement opportunities and the first one's ending-save checkpoint independently of whether a route will be issued or executed. An already-underway turn or attached phase when the effect establishes is neither future opportunity and grants no retrospective route or early save. At the first recorded eligible future regular END, or the END of the first actual future original-owner attached phase for an attached companion, offer this application's one early STR ending save if it still exists and the original expiry has not occurred. This END save requires neither a successful START instruction nor actual travel. Suppression at that START, no conscious/perceiving caster, Grappled/Speed zero, an unavailable route or a lost movement budget cannot postpone the checkpoint to a later opportunity or remove the save. The existing scheduled-save-during-suppression rule also applies when suppression continues across this END. A successful save ends this application; failure leaves only its original remaining opportunity and original deadline. At the second original END, expiry occurs first and no redundant final save is rolled. Missing real companion phases create no extra phase, order, movement, ordinary START/END trigger or resource refresh; no END-only substitute for an absent attached phase is granted by this Puppet-only completion. Preserve the original maximum/expiry marker under the existing timing contract. In EN6-03-B, release at 2.2 excludes the underway phase ending 2.4; suppression over START 8 loses that route, but END 8.4 still offers the original early STR save, and expiry stays 14.4.

CTRL15-GEAS-SOFT-01 — scoped authored completion for Geas only. Record at establishment whether this application actually acquired its whole-Action component. That permission cannot grow later because an ordinary door locks, a free handoff becomes a second object interaction, an encounter changes, a rest restores another allowance, or an implementation finds an easier method requiring a full Action. An application admitted only as a meaningful soft mandate may compel only that original mandate's lawful soft movement/posture/ordinary-interaction portion. It may use another actually available safe method within that same permission or wait for a genuine ordinary opening. If none is currently executable, suspend the unexecutable portion under Geas's existing temporary-obstacle rule; retain the original objective and deadline, not a deferred hard-control claim or a new objective. A separately voluntary Action remains voluntary and is not granted or paid by Geas; if it opens a lawful soft path, the original soft instruction can continue. A genuinely new hard Geas requires a new legal paid casting, actual admission and the applicable hard-control check at that establishment. This does not import Mass Suggestion's distinct ending rule, erase an already admitted hard Geas, shorten thirty days, forbid essential rest/care or create catch-up work.

CTRL15-DOMINATE-PHASE-01 — NEW scoped attached-body completion for Dominate Monster only, not an automatic extension of Dominate Beast, Dominate Person or Confusion. This paragraph applies only after the recipient independently meets this spell's actual documented operative CR-at-most-10 predicate and all other admission rules. It assigns no CR or former wild profile to a bounded companion. For a genuinely eligible owner-attached body, use only its existing original-owner regular attached phase for a future mental-order opportunity, after that phase's required processing. Preserve the original owner's actual structural command/offense limits and any legally reusable pending reservation for this same body and same phase; no owner's involuntary Bonus Action payment, new controller allowance, stolen other-body reservation, independent turn or extra phase is created. At the END of each actually affected original-owner regular attached phase, including the upcoming END of a phase already underway at admission, offer the spell's WIS ending save even if no order was issued or executed. Such an underway phase supplies an END save but no retrospective START order. These are this spell's specific checkpoints, not ordinary creature START/END, death saves, recharge, Reaction refresh or another effect's periodic tick. If no real attached execution sequence exists, allow only an END-only WIS schedule at admission +6 seconds and then six-second intervals up to the original sixty-second maximum; it grants no orders or Actions. Store the timestamp of the last resolved ending save, initially using the admission timestamp as the cadence anchor. With no real phase sequence, the next END-only save is the first strictly future six-second marker measured from that anchor; missed past markers do not produce catch-up saves. A real regular phase END consumes the next unresolved save opportunity and becomes the new cadence anchor. Switching into real phases maps that next opportunity to the next actual regular phase END, not to an immediate transition save. Switching out uses the stored anchor, not the transition time, so toggling phase availability cannot continually reset the six-second interval. At a simultaneous phase END and END-only marker, process one source save and consume that same opportunity once. No switch replays a resolved save or changes the original absolute deadline. Expiry wins at its exact deadline. This save bridge leaves both native-profile content dependencies in EN5-01-A and EN5-01-B conditional.

CTRL15-READY-SELECTION-01 — Control15 routing clarification of the already accepted ordinary Ready contract. Generic shared wording that selects named targets, ordered target lists or a target-centered area at commitment describes a direct casting; it does not override ordinary Ready's express target/area selection at release. A legal Ready preparation fixes the spell, acquired school/version, mode and other actual preparation-bound choices, pays its casting transaction and resolves its single counter window. Its legal target, ordered target list or area point is selected at release before that release's hidden eligibility/outcome checks; target-dependent initial geometry and recipient HP snapshots use the actual release/resolution state, never a setup-time ghost target. Source-specific already-fixed commands, appearance choices and modes cannot be rewritten from hidden release results. All actual perception, line of effect, comprehension and other source predicates still apply when required. This grants no retroactive hearing, free command utterance, new communication channel, second casting/payment, second counter window or access to a missing Action-time source. The trigger completes before the response. An invalid or declined release spends no release Reaction and may wait only within its existing Ready deadline; setup costs remain spent. No text concerning an originally immediate spell establishes its field, damage, control clock or target condition while its energy is merely held. Effect duration begins at actual establishment unless that exact source expressly states a different clock; capture/permission/Ready deadlines retain their own independent earlier limits.

COPY-READY-ALLOWANCE-01 — NEW scoped decision for the seven FS-08/SUP-07 feat-copy profiles only. This does not change ordinary Ready, ordinary class spell cadence, the Mirrorsage class Echo implementation, any profile's payload or any acquisition predicate.

PREPARATION. A direct feat-copy cast retains its current commitment-round allowance rule. A Readied feat-copy also requires the owner's feat-copy allowance in its actual preparation numbered round. If this owner actually has the separately acquired Mirrorsage shared-release engine to which the exact source binds feat copies, require that same round's actual class allowance as well; an ability route alone never invents the engine. Validate all presently required setup predicates first. At one authoritative legal preparation commitment, atomically spend the Action, quote/payment, permission/use, feat-copy round allowance and any required actually owned class allowance, provide components, update the independent feat-copy chronological family/strain exactly once, and establish the one Ready concentration burden. These spends occur before the preparation counter window. Either all required allowance/resources are valid before commitment or no new setup spend occurs; a partial class/feat-ledger reservation is forbidden. A countered, replaced, expired or concentration-lost preparation retains its actual committed spends. It cannot refund the consumed Mimicry use, restore displaced concentration or free that preparation round for another copy. A genuinely failed precommit validation is not a paid preparation.

HELD RECORD. Bind one unique preparation ID, actual owner, fixed captured source/profile/q/mode, paid transaction and consumed permission receipt, preparation round, affected ledger identities, original Ready expiry and any independently applicable earlier source/capture deadline. A new valid Ready may replace it only under ordinary Ready; an illegal replacement attempt cannot delete it. Consuming the capture permission at preparation is not itself loss of this paid hold's authorization, but this completion does not extend a printed earlier capture/use/hold deadline or create a new permission. No allowance in a future round is reserved ahead of time. No payload or success-triggered effect has happened merely because setup was paid. Capture validity, source component availability and upstream providers still require their actual existing records; this decision is not a missing-source adapter.

RELEASE. After a real perceivable trigger has completed and before the Ready's original expiry, perform the ordinary release legality check, including an actually available lawful Reaction and all applicable source/target/geometry predicates. Check the ACTUAL RELEASE numbered round's feat-copy allowance and any actually required class shared-release allowance. In the same numbered round as preparation, reuse only this same held preparation's already-spent allowance tokens, not another copy's tokens. In a later numbered round, both applicable release-round allowances must be free and are atomically spent together with the Reaction when this release commits. The preparation-round spends are not moved, refunded or reclassified. Thus cross-round Ready deliberately occupies one attempt allowance in each touched round, but pays RP, capture permission, components, strain and casting history only once. This is the selected conservative timing choice, not a claim that the prior source already specified it. It prevents both preparation spam after a counter and a deferred copy plus a competing copy bypassing the release-round cap. An unowned class engine is still not granted.

If the trigger is declined, target is invalid, an actual prerequisite is missing or either required release-round allowance is unavailable, do not spend the Reaction or partially debit another ledger; keep the existing held record only until another lawful occurrence before its original expiry. Supply no hidden-target or item-identification diagnostic. A genuinely permitted competing direct copy or class release may use its available round allowance first; holding a prior-round copy gives no priority or override. If nothing legal can release before expiry, the hold is lost normally. At the exact expiry boundary, expiry occurs first.

On a valid release commitment, consume the hold once before resolving its one payload. No second RP/material payment, source-permission consumption, casting-family/Refrain update, ordinary cast hook or Counterspell window occurs. Later prevention of that committed payload does not refund the Reaction or release-round allowances. Replay/retry of the same release ID cannot create another payload or another spend. Immediate Strike/Burst/Mend/Step releases end the Ready concentration after resolution. Sustained Ward/Hindrance/Boon continue the same one burden with their real effect clock and earlier source limits; there is no second slot. Save/load must preserve the complete hold identity, original expiry, consumed receipts, chronology and per-owner/per-numbered-round ledger entries. Extra turns, reloading, relabeling a round, changing a qualifying route or swapping captured profile names cannot reset them. This settles only allowance/transaction timing; complete Ready scheduling, perception, source-specific payloads and live engine behavior still require implementation and tests.
